summary: The saturday-playwright-leaflet package ships a LeafletFixture Playwright fixture with 11 documented helpers but has no tests of its own; its test script is a literal exit 1 that breaks the monorepo-wide `pnpm -r test`. This order adds a self-contained fixture page under fixtures/ (local Leaflet assets, a local image tile, known markers/polygon/layer control, exposing window.__SATURDAY_LEAFLET_MAP__), a Playwright suite covering every README helper against known fixture values, and the config to run that suite in real Chrome inside the saturday-runner:debian image with --network none — establishing the pattern the Cesium package will later follow. Doing so surfaces a real defect: src/fixture.ts currently loads Turf.js from a public CDN at test time, which cannot work offline, so that load must move to the package's own local @turf/turf dependency as part of this fix.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Given packages/saturday-playwright-leaflet/fixtures/, a static page MUST load Leaflet from the package's own dependencies (no CDN), a local image, and a known set of markers carrying saturdayMetadata, a polygon, and a layer control, and MUST expose window.__SATURDAY_LEAFLET_MAP__.
examples: fixtures/index.html references leaflet.js and leaflet.css from the package's own node_modules/leaflet/dist, never a CDN URL
At least 3 markers, each with marker.saturdayMetadata = { id, name }
One L.polygon with fixed, known coordinates
One L.control.layers overlay with a fixed, known name
window.__SATURDAY_LEAFLET_MAP__ is set once the map and all layers finish loading

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Given the package's test script, it MUST serve the fixture page and run a Playwright suite with at least one test per helper documented in README.md, and each test MUST assert a known value taken from the fixture.
examples: waitForMapLoad, getCenter, getBounds, getMarkers, drawLine, getMarkersAlongLine, distanceBetween, isPointInPolygon, assertPopupContent, isLayerVisible, checkTileFailures — all 11 README helpers get at least one test

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Given each helper's test, it MUST fail when the fixture's corresponding value is changed; the delivery record MUST document, per helper, the fixture change made and the resulting failing output.

Given the suite, it MUST run in real Chrome (channel: 'chrome') inside the runner image with no network, and MUST pass with the literal docker command below after dependencies are installed and the package is built; the delivery record MUST capture that command's output.
examples: docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --network none -v "$PWD:/work" saturday-runner:debian bash -lc 'cd /work && pnpm --filter @orieken/saturday-playwright-leaflet test'

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Given the change is complete, every new or changed function MUST have cyclomatic complexity below 7, every changed line MUST be covered by a test that can fail, and no file outside scope.paths MUST change except the run's own delivery record under docs/features/leaflet-package-tests/.

newDependencies: @turf/turf — added to packages/saturday-playwright-leaflet's own dependencies, replacing the CDN-loaded turf.min.js in src/fixture.ts; required because AC4 runs the suite with --network none and the current page.addScriptTag CDN URL cannot load offline
architecturalFlags: No architect needed: this is additive test-infrastructure work inside one existing package, following an established pattern (apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/playwright.config.ts's chrome/runner-image project) — no new package, base class, or layer boundary change.

src/fixture.ts's `leaflet` fixture currently injects Turf.js from a public CDN (`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@turf/turf@6/turf.min.js`) via page.addScriptTag. AC4 requires the suite to pass under `--network none`; this load will fail offline and break every helper depending on window.turf (getMarkersAlongLine, isPointInPolygon, distanceBetween). This is in scope to fix (scope.paths covers src/fixture.ts, and pnpm-lock.yaml is already listed in scope.paths, consistent with adding a new dependency) even though it isn't literally one of the spec's named ACs — AC4 cannot pass without it.
Removing the CDN script load is also a minor supply-chain improvement: the suite no longer fetches arbitrary third-party JS over the network at test time.

checkTileFailures() detects failures via the DOM class `.leaflet-tile-loaded.leaflet-tile-error`, not network interception. The fixture's tile layer must point at a local image (AC1) for the happy-path test; the failing-path test (AC3 — must fail when the fixture value changes) needs a deliberately broken local URL (e.g. a 404 against the fixture's own static server), not an external network URL, since the suite runs with --network none.

fixture.ts exposes 13 methods; README documents only 11 (dragMap and zoomMap are undocumented). AC2 only requires one test per README-documented helper, so dragMap/zoomMap are not required by this order and remain uncovered after this change — flagged for a future order, not a gap in this one.

openQuestions: Should the Playwright suite import the fixture from the package's built dist/ output or from src/ directly? AC4's docker command runs test only after the package 'is built' — recommend importing via the package's own published entry (as apps/ye-olde-magic-shop already does) so a stale build can't silently pass; needs a developer decision.

The exact local-serving path for @turf/turf's browser bundle inside node_modules is version-dependent — developer must verify the installed version's bundle layout (or build one, e.g. with esbuild) before wiring the script tag.

Should the new chrome project run headless or under Xvfb like ye-olde-magic-shop's? Leaflet needs no WebGL (unlike the Cesium rationale for that config's GL launch args), so the simplest option that passes AC4's docker command should be preferred.
